references.text: Joshua is commanded to meditate on the Book of the Law day and night, reflecting the king's duty to copy and read the law daily.
Joshua wrote a copy of Moses' law on stones, illustrating the practice of copying the law mentioned in Deuteronomy.
David exhorts Solomon to keep the Lord's laws as written in the law of Moses, reflecting the king's responsibility to follow the law.
The discovery of the Book of the Law in the temple during King Josiah's reign highlights the importance of the written law and its authority for the king.
The Book of the Law was found in the house of the Lord, leading to reform, underscoring the significance of the law for the kingdom.
The psalmist's love for the law and meditation on it all day reflects the king's call to study the law continuously.
Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the Levitical priests to preserve. This is the background for why the king should receive his copy from the priests.
Moses finished writing the words of the law in a book and gave it to the Levites for safekeeping beside the ark of the covenant.
